A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Color Equivariant Network by the same authors. All main-text material and Appendices A–C are readable and matchable, including equations, figures and result tables.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification experiments on Hue-shift MNIST, 3D Shapes, Camelyon17 and CIFAR-10 in Tables 1–4, plus representation analyses and color sorting.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results in Tables 1–4 and the corresponding representation analyses and sorting demonstration.

M1.justification: The HSL input transformations, lifting procedure, group convolutions and final group pooling are unchanged in Section 4 and Appendix B. No algorithmic or architectural component is added or revised.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same four datasets and retain the same global/local hue shifts, hospital distribution shift, natural color variation and automobile sorting task.

E2.justification: Comparator membership matches within every table: Z2CNN and CEConv/CEConv-2 for MNIST; ResNet18, ResNet44, CNN and CEConv comparisons for 3D Shapes; ResNet50 for Camelyon17; and ResNet44/CEConv for CIFAR-10.

E3.justification: Sections 5.1–5.4 and Appendix B retain the same splits, classification-error metric, saturation discretizations, preprocessing, training budgets and optimization settings. The parameter-unit correction in Table 4 does not document a changed model configuration.

E4.justification: The MNIST trajectory and feature-map analyses, saturation-discretization comparisons and automobile sorting demonstration are retained. Their figures are relocated or renumbered, with no new ablation, robustness test or case study.

E5.justification: Appendix B retains three seeds (1999–2001) for MNIST, 3D Shapes and CIFAR-10, and five seeds (1997–2001) for Camelyon17. Parenthetical uncertainty reporting is unchanged.

E6.justification: Table 4 corrects the Sat-d1 and Sat-d2 parameter entries from '2.55' in v1 to '2.55M' in v2. Classification errors, uncertainty values, rankings and qualitative findings otherwise match; no performance improvement is reported.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, group actions, lifting-equivariance derivation, sorting-distance expression and Appendix C proofs are retained. Equations 1–36 undergo layout changes without substantive mathematical revision.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims: hue/saturation equivariance without increased parameter requirements, competitive classification under color variation, and interpretable representations supporting color sorting.

C2.justification: The explanations linking robustness to representation structure are unchanged. Section 6.1 retains the same luminance qualification, computational-cost limitation, finite-group approximation limitation and proposed Fourier-series direction.

D1.justification: Table 4 clarifies that Sat-d1 and Sat-d2 have 2.55 million parameters by restoring missing units. Appendix B's implementation, architecture, hyperparameter and hardware disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The same 36 cited works and the same positioning against prior color-equivariant networks remain. Reference reordering and bibliographic metadata changes do not alter the cited research or novelty arguments.

P1.justification: v2 adds Section 7 acknowledgements, revises the author block and fixes isolated typos, including 'unchanced' to 'unchanged'. Scientific prose and section order are largely identical. Reference 29 acquires malformed author formatting and loses its venue/year information.

P2.justification: The entire document adopts two columns. v1 Figure 1's panels become separate, enlarged Figures 1 and 2 in different locations; Tables 1, 3 and 4 are transposed or restructured. Existing figures, captions and appendix displays are extensively resized and repositioned.

improvement.justification: v2 corrects two parameter-unit omissions and modestly improves presentation through larger introductory diagrams and simpler table layouts. The scientific evidence and proofs remain unchanged. Reference 29's reduced bibliographic quality is a small regression, but the overall gains in clarity support a limited improvement.
